title: AI Replacing Workers Will Take 10 Years And Job Loss Will Be 5%: Nobel Laureate Daron Acemoglu
key_facts: Nobel laureate and MIT professor Daron Acemoglu believes AI-led job replacement could take at least ten years, with only about 5% of people replaced when it happens.
Acemoglu's essay appeared in the first issue of The Humanist Review, published by Microsoft AI (MAI); Mustafa Suleyman, Microsoft's CEO of AI, quoted it in a LinkedIn post.
Acemoglu says AI has not yet shown up in productivity statistics, and expects roughly 1.5% added to GDP over ten years (as quoted by Suleyman).
He says the last 1% of accuracy is the hard part of full automation, and that tasks in the lab are not yet proven in the wild.
He argues for 'pro-worker AI' that makes humans better at their jobs rather than replacing them.
The article says Microsoft AI released a 'Code of Conduct' for future models for public consultation.
quote_evidence: Nobel laureate and MIT professor Daron Acemoglu believes that such a scenario could take at least ten years to play out and when it does only about 5% of humans would be replaced by artificial intelligence-led chatbots or similar other products.
Rather than pursuing full-scale automation, build AI that makes humans better at their jobs and creates new skills and expertise for them, he adds.
why_it_matters_hint: An economist argues AI job losses will be slow and small, while the headline presents his forecast as fact.
notes: Headline overstated: it states 'will take 10 years' and 'job loss will be 5%' as fact; the essay says 'could take at least ten years' and 'only about 5%'. Score lowered 5 to 4 (-1). Source chain: CXOToday reports on Acemoglu's essay (The Humanist Review) quoted in Suleyman's post; the cookie banner was ignored. Text is an opinion essay, so kept as analysis.
